notes.note: Reviewed the changed handoff, cold-context, saved-fork and external-client contracts against foreground execution, lineage, EventStore and the real runtime route composition. Native identity comes from the prepared invocation; derived witness failure cannot erase a terminal. Saved forks have no Session until first send; metadata display does not mutate the pin. Local evidence: 830 core owner tests, 34 witness/pin tests, 132 conversation-route cases, and the retained guard mutation. Live providers, installed-client onboarding and two-account selection/application remain NOT_VERIFIED.

Reviewed the fork-ready wire arm and SDK parser against the server open route and dock policy/controller. The new arm carries a saved transcript but no currentSessionId or execution binding; pending start is busy and writable first-send eligibility is distinct from an established Session. The parser refuses invented runtime bindings. SDK/dock/recovery-notice tests and UI typechecking passed; no browser or live-provider result is claimed.

Reviewed the added orchestration receipt/open shapes, context-unavailable classification, optional fork context digest and the owning station-control-external-client subpath. Its selected-tool vocabulary, lease/config DTO and pure environment-free untrusted-response parser confer no authority; issuer and runtime owners enforce file-proven operator, current access and scope. No grant/browser assurance or provider qualification is inferred from these types.

Reviewed mcp-clients authorize/create/revoke, registration/help and the explicit-api-base response parser. Output is exclusive POSIX 0600, contains no operator credential, and stdout omits bearer/config. Write failure makes one exact lease compensation attempt; unknown issuance/revoke outcomes are not success or automatic retries. Request timeout remains per request with no total command cap; Windows create refuses. The Codex recipe clears inherited Station/provider credentials. CLI local tests passed with one Windows-only skip; installed-client and live-account acceptance remain unverified.

Reviewed only the changed continuity and local external-client ownership clauses and their linked production callers. Saved fork/context/witness data remains in the existing EventStore; real Sessions start on first send. Ordinary reuse requires exact completed seed evidence, and native subject identity is captured before effect. The public setup/revoke surface reuses the existing MCP transport and preserves delegated custody and per-tool policy. Existing unrelated module claims/owner notes are preserved, not newly attested by this review. Local proving owners pass; live/provider/account and independent branch review are not implied.

Reviewed the continuation additions against actual Session start/send/resume guards, lineage and private witness persistence. A saved fork is an independent Conversation; handoff retains its Conversation. A consumed start is not a seed acknowledgement; native identity is invocation-bound and failed projections preserve terminal facts while withholding context proof. Existing Flow, lifecycle and tool-policy ownership is unchanged. The 830 core and 34 witness/pin local owners pass; no installed-provider or two-account acceptance is claimed.

Reviewed the narrow personal-host client surface against current issuer, real DevicePairing credentialHoldsScope composition, token registry, caller derivation and runtime mount. File-proven local operator plus access:manage is required; current authority is checked after body and during verification. Tools are explicit and TTL is 60..3600; recorded Session/Project binding is not liveness. Header-only loopback leases remain delegated custody, independent of runtime rotation; revocation/expiry/restart and per-tool ownership restrictions remain. Existing browser/plugin consent and bound-browser requirements are unchanged. Local API/CLI evidence and prior bounded policy review do not establish remote OAuth/TLS, a live client or two-account qualification.
